scope: Round 3. Only the roles named in SRS.txt sections 3.19-3.21: Staff (statistics and report) and Admin (system administration: user management and security). Customer appears only as a login subject in sec-001; no new customer features. Roles map to the existing users.role column (default 'customer'); this round adds the values 'staff' and 'admin'.

roles.staff: An internal user who views auction statistics and exports reports.
roles.admin: A system administrator who manages users, roles, permissions and passwords.

features.title: One login page for customer, staff and admin
features.user_visible_behavior: Customers, staff and admins sign in on the same login page. After login each lands on their own home: customer on the existing dashboard, staff on the statistics page, admin on the user management page. The navigation only shows links the user's role can use.
verification: Seed: npm run db:seed -w be creates one staff and one admin account (credentials documented in docs/).
Unit: the JWT and /api/me include the user's role.
API: login as each of customer, staff and admin returns 200 and the correct role.
E2E: logging in as staff lands on /staff/statistics; as admin lands on /admin/users; as customer lands on the existing dashboard.
E2E: a customer does not see Staff or Admin links in the navigation.

features.title: Role-based permissions on resources
features.user_visible_behavior: Each role has a set of permissions (for example 'report.view', 'report.export', 'user.manage'). Staff and admin pages and APIs check the permission; a user without it gets 403 from the API and a 'not allowed' page in the UI. An admin can view the permission matrix and grant or revoke a permission for a role.
verification: Unit: requirePermission middleware allows a user whose role has the permission and rejects others with 403.
API: a customer calling a staff report endpoint gets 403; staff gets 200; anonymous gets 401.
API: a customer or staff calling an admin user endpoint gets 403; admin gets 200.
API: admin revokes 'report.export' from staff, then staff export returns 403; granting it back restores 200.
API: admin cannot remove 'user.manage' from the admin role (prevents lockout).
E2E: admin opens the permission screen, toggles a permission for staff, and the staff user's access changes accordingly.
evidence: 2026-10-18 Migration 20261018055638_role_permissions: permissions + role_permissions tables with default grants (staff: report.view, report.export; admin: user.manage, permission.manage); seed re-adds missing defaults

API: a locked user gets a clear error on login; unlocking restores login.

API: deleting a user with an active auction or active bid returns 409 with a reason.
API: deleting yourself returns 400.
E2E: admin deletes a user through the confirm dialog and the row disappears.

features.title: Filter and list auctions for statistics
features.user_visible_behavior: On the statistics page staff pick a from date, a to date and an auction status (all, upcoming, active, ended, cancelled) and see every matching auction with title, seller, start and end time, status, starting price, final price, winner and commission. A summary row shows the count and totals.
verification: API: GET /api/staff/auctions?from&to&status returns only auctions in the range with that status; totals match the rows.
API: from after to, or an invalid date or status, returns 400.
API: the date range is inclusive of both days (assumption: filter on auction start time).
E2E: staff sets a range and status, submits, and the table shows the seeded matching auctions and the correct count.
features.notes: Which date the range filters on (start, end or created) is not stated in the SRS; assumed start_time. Status uses the effective status, same as the rest of the app.

features.title: Export the statistics list to Excel
features.user_visible_behavior: Staff click 'Export to Excel' and download an .xlsx file holding the same rows and summary that the current filter shows, with a header row and the filter range in the file name.
verification: API: GET /api/staff/auctions/export with the same filters returns an .xlsx content type and attachment header.
Unit: parsing the generated workbook gives a header row plus one row per auction matching the list endpoint.
E2E: staff click Export and a file named like auctions_<from>_<to>.xlsx downloads.
features.notes: Requires an xlsx library on the backend (e.g. exceljs).

features.title: Chart of the statistics
features.user_visible_behavior: Under the filter, a chart shows the number of auctions per day in the selected range broken down by status, and a second chart shows final sale value per day. The charts update when the filter changes and show an empty state when nothing matches.
verification: API: GET /api/staff/auctions/summary returns per-day counts by status and per-day sale value; the counts add up to the list total.
E2E: after filtering, the chart renders with data points for the seeded days; with a range that has no auctions, the empty state shows.
features.notes: Requires a chart library on the frontend (e.g. recharts).

features.title: Revenue and customer statistics
features.user_visible_behavior: For the selected date range staff see system revenue (sum of commission from settled auctions) and customer figures: new registrations, number of active bidders and sellers, and the top 5 sellers and bidders by value. These figures are included in the Excel export as a second sheet.
verification: API: GET /api/staff/revenue?from&to returns total commission equal to the sum of auction_settlements.commission_amount in the range.
API: GET /api/staff/customers?from&to returns registrations, active bidder and seller counts and top-5 lists matching seeded data.
E2E: staff see the revenue and customer cards for a range with seeded settlements.
features.notes: SRS marks this as optional ('You can...'). Do it last.
